items.title: The US wants to block China from renting AI power abroad but China already built a parallel supply chain from US AI output
items.description: The US is tightening its chip export controls. Data centers in third countries like Singapore and Malaysia will soon need a US license to buy Nvidia chips, closing the loophole that let Chinese firms rent cloud compute abroad. A Reuters investigation also reveals how China offsets its hardware shortage through industrial-scale distillation of US AI models. items.title: OpenAI opens its cybersecurity tool Daybreak to NATO and European governments
items.description: OpenAI is opening its cybersecurity tool Daybreak to NATO and several European governments, including Germany, France, and Poland. The EU's cybersecurity agency ENISA has already used it to find real vulnerabilities in EU software. The NATO Communications and Information Agency (NCIA) says it's already making heavy use of the underlying models. The article OpenAI opens its cybersecurity tool Daybreak to NATO and European governments appeared first on The Decoder .

items.title: Reports of AI-generated child sexual abuse material have surged more than 8,400 percent in two years
items.description: Edinburgh's Childlight Institute reports a more than 8,400 percent increase in AI-generated child sexual abuse material over two years, from about 4,700 reports in 2023 to over 400,000 in 2025. Abusers are using tools like nudify apps for blackmail. Childlight CEO Paul Stanfield wants governments to classify the problem as a preventable public health emergency.
